$comment: The main-screen UI theme, replayed onto every upstream checkout by tools/patch_ui.py.
Why a replayed patch instead of editing the checkout: build/ is gitignored, and
tools/build_apk.sh resets it to the pinned upstream revision before every build
(prepare_fork does git reset --hard && git clean -fdxq). Any hand edit made under
build/ survives exactly zero builds. This file is tracked; patch_ui.py re-applies it.
THE FROST IS SIMULATED, NOT BLURRED. AndroidManifest.xml declares minSdkVersion 10
(Android 2.3.7). Real backdrop blur needs RenderScript (API 11+) or RenderEffect
(API 31+); neither exists at this target, and the camera body would not ship the
runtime anyway. So a 'frosted glass' bar is what it was before blur existed: a
translucent layer, a faint gradient sheen, and rounded inner corners that read as a
glass slab. Kept at high opacity (~0.90) on purpose - the underlying camera frame is
arbitrarily bright or dark, and at high enough alpha the composite stays light, so
the dark text below keeps its contrast over any scene. Lower the alpha and this
stops being guaranteed.
Colours are #AARRGGBB: one string feeds Android XML directly and becomes a Java
literal by swapping # for 0x, so this file is the only place a colour is written.
Two keys decide what is ON SCREEN rather than what colour it is. Both are kept as
toggles rather than deleted from the layout, because each is the sort of thing you
only miss once it is gone:
legend_visibility   'gone' hides the key legend - the row of glyphs and labels
under the chips saying which body key does what. Navigation
here is the camera's wheel and dial, there is no touchscreen,
so that row is the ONLY on-screen reminder that ENTER stores
the recipe and AEL/DISP cycles the overlay. Set it back to
'visible' to get it back. The view stays declared either way:
MainActivity calls hints.setMode() on it and would crash on a
view that is not there.
app_title_visibility  the small app name at the far left of the top bar.
tag_visibility       'gone' hides the CS / PE chip that sits behind the recipe name.
It is NOT decoration and it is NOT a key - it is a mode readout.
MainActivity writes it as edit[R_PE] != 0 ? "PE" : "CS":
CS = Creative Style, the camera's own look engine (contrast,
saturation, sharpness), which is what the bulk of these recipes
are and which survives into RAW. PE = Picture Effect, a filter
that only lands on JPEG - the app says so outright ('RAW is on:
effect ignored') and picking one forces quality to JPEG Fine.
So the chip answers 'is what I am looking at baked into the RAW
or only into the JPEG', which is the one thing you cannot tell
from the name. Kept visible; set to 'gone' to drop it.
font_regular / font_bold — a rounded face, because this target has none.
minSdkVersion is 10, and Gingerbread ships Droid Sans and little
else: there is no rounded system font to ask for, and
android:fontFamily / res/font are API 26. So the face is bundled
as a raw asset under assets/fonts/ and bound to the views in Java
by tools/patch_ui.py. Two consequences worth knowing:
(1) the packaging step must carry -A assets, or aapt never puts
the .ttf in the APK. patch_ui edits build.sh and build.cmd to
add it. If that edit ever stops matching, the app does NOT
crash - it quietly falls back to the system font, which is
the one failure mode here with no error message at all.
(2) each APK grows by roughly the size of the two .ttf files.
Bundled: Quicksand (SIL OFL 1.1), Regular + Bold, ~157 KB the
pair. To swap it, drop another OFL pair into assets/fonts/ and
change these two names — nothing else needs to move.
